title: If I had known
goal: Talk about a past that didn't happen, and what would have followed, with -sAydI.

intro.text: For a past that didn't happen, add `-(y)DI` to `-sA`: *Bilseydim gelirdim* (If I had known, I'd have come). The main clause keeps `-(I)rdI`, so the if-clause tells you whether it's about now or then.

vocab.en: to know about, to have heard (haberim yok: I don't know about it)

exercises.question: *Bilseydim gelirdim.* What does it mean?
options: If I had known, I would have come.

why.1: That would be *Bilirsem gelirim*, a real condition.
why.2: That would be *Bildiğim için geldim*: a fact, not a past that didn't happen.

exercises.explain: `-sAydI` in the if-clause: the speaker didn't know, so didn't come.

exercises.label: *gelmek* + `-sAydI`: if I had come, if you had come…
exercises.explain: `-sA`, the buffer y, `-DI`, then the type II ending: *gel-se-y-di-m*. For **they**, *gelselerdi* or *gelseydiler*.

exercises.text: Bana önceden haber ___ seni havalimanında karşılardım.
exercises.en: If you had let me know in advance, I would have met you at the airport.

reject.why: *Verirsen* is a real condition about the future. Here the past didn't happen: *verseydin*.
*Versen* is heard in speech for this, but the standard form for a past that didn't happen is *verseydin*.
*Verdiysen* means **if you did let me know**: a real past. You didn't, so *verseydin*.

exercises.hint: *Haber vermek*: put *vermek* in the unreal past, for **you**.
exercises.explain: *ver-se-y-di-n*: if you had let me know. The main clause, *karşılardım*, keeps `-(I)rdI`.

accept: If we had left early, we would not have missed the train.
If we had left earlier, we would not have missed the train.
If we'd left [early|earlier], we would not have missed the train.
We would not have missed the train if [we had|we'd] left [early|earlier].
If we had [set off|gone out] [early|earlier], we would not have missed the train.

exercises.prompt: If you had told me, I would have helped you.

reject.why: After `-sAydI`, the main clause needs `-(I)rdI`: *ederdim*. *Ederim* is a present habit.

exercises.explain: *söyle-se-y-di-n*: if you had told me. *Yardım ederdim* (or *edecektim*): I would have helped.

exercises.en: If we had waited a little longer, we would have seen him.

exercises.prompt: If you had seen that film, you would have liked it.

exercises.explain: Negative *-ma*, conditional *-sa*, buffer *y*, past *-dı*, ending *-k*. Harmony keeps every vowel back.

exercises.question: Which main clause fits? *Dün akşam gelseydin…*

why.1: The aorist describes a habit or a later possibility, not a past that didn't happen.
why.2: The future can't follow a past that didn't happen.

exercises.explain: *Gelseydin … görürdün*: if you'd come last night, you'd have seen Ayşe.

accept: If I had known, I would have picked you up at the airport.
If I had known, I would have picked you up from the airport.
If I'd known, I would have picked you up [at|from] the airport.
I would have picked you up [at|from] the airport if [I had|I'd] known.
If I had known about it, I would have picked you up [at|from] the airport.

exercises.task: Think of three things that went differently last year from what you wanted. For each one, write what would have happened if…, with `-sAydI` and `-(I)rdI`.
models: Daha erken başvursaydım o işi alırdım. Sınavdan önce daha çok çalışsaydım sınavı geçerdim. Yazın İzmir'e gitseydim arkadaşlarımı görürdüm.
Otobüsü kaçırmasaydım iş görüşmesine geç kalmazdım. Vaktim olsaydı her hafta yüzmeye giderdim. Seni önceden uyarsaydım bu kaza olmazdı.
checklist: Each if-clause ends in `-sAydI` and an ending: *başvursaydım*, *gitseydim*
Nouns, adjectives and *var* go through *olmak*: *vaktim olsaydı*

exercises.en: If you had come, you would have seen.

exercises.prompt: If I had applied earlier, I would have gotten the job.
accept: Ben daha erken başvursaydım [işi|o işi|bu işi] [alırdım|alacaktım].
exercises.explain: *başvur-sa-y-dı-m*: if I had applied. *İşi alırdım*: I would have gotten the job.
